docs.title: 4. Addressing Gaps
docs.text: The section will check if the insurance company has thought of ways to detect and address potential the mismatch between the index and their losses. It will also estimate the gap due to this misalignment in monetary value to guide any efforts to compensate farmers for losses not covered by the index.

docs.title: a. Do you have a system in place to detect the mismatch?
docs.text: Follow up: If yes, how would you detect it? Potential answers: (e.g., farmer hotline to request for an audit, scheduled visits to farmers, etc.)

docs.title: b. What grievance and remedy mechanisms do you have in place to ensure payouts align with actual farmer losses or compensate farmers for actual losses, if any?
docs.text: Potential answers: (e.g., ex-gratia payments, satellite-based plus audits, contingency fund, etc.)

docs.title: c. How big is the gap between what payouts would have been and farmer payout expectations in monetary value?
docs.text: Follow up: Is this a gap you could include in the design of the product?

docs.title: 3. Alignment of Payouts with Farmer Losses
docs.text: The section will look at how well the chosen index for the insurance matches farmer's experience of losses. There is a follow up question for weather-based index insurance around when measurements will be taken since this decides payout.

docs.title: a. How well does what payouts would have been align with farmer payout expectations based on your chosen index?
docs.text: Follow-up: How often does payout align and not align with farmer expectation?

docs.title: b. During which part/s of the season will satellite or rainfall measurements be taken to determine payouts (for weather-based index insurance)?
docs.text: Follow-up: What sources will you base these on?

docs.title: 5. Farmer Communication
docs.text: This section will assess the company’s work in 1) communicating and educating farmers about insurance, 2) monitoring outputs from these communication and training efforts, and 3) handling complaints and grievances, to make the insurance product truly valuable for farmers. These questions will primarily be qualitative with verification through submission of documents (training plans, questionnaires, etc.)

docs.title: a. Communications Strategy
docs.text:
• In the past, have you established ways to communicate and train farmers about their insurance? If yes, who did the communication and training? What activities were done?
  • For the proposed product, what is your planned communication and training strategy? Who will do the communication and training? What activities will be done?

docs.title: b. Monitoring Strategy
docs.text:
• In the past, did you check that farmers understood that they had insurance and what they can expect from the product? If yes, how did you do so?
  • For the proposed product, how do you plan to check that farmers understand the insurance and set their expectations about the product?

docs.title: c. Grievance and remedy mechanisms:
docs.text:
• In the past, did you have grievance and remedy mechanisms in place for farmers who experience losses but did not receive payouts? If yes, what mechanisms did you have in place?
  • For the proposed contract, what grievance and remedy mechanisms will you put in place for farmers who experience losses but did not receive payouts?

docs.title: 1. Insurance Program Structure and Providers
docs.text: The Assessment will begin with a series of qualitative questions that will 1) identify what the insurance program aims to achieve and set the baseline for evaluating responses throughout the assessment, and 2) gather background of the Providers

docs.title: a. Structure of the Insurance Program
docs.text:
These questions will set the stage for the insurance requirements of the contracting entity. Before proceeding with the rest of the assessment tool, these questions should be answered by the contracting entity for the insurance. This will ground the discussion and help in assessment of some of the quantitative questions in this tool.

  • What is the insurance product meant to cover? Potential answers: - Protect farmers from catastrophic events - Provide guarantees for loans - Cover the cost of inputs - Other?

  • How is the insurance program funded/structured? Potential answers - National insurance program with government subsidy - Contract farming with a food manufacturer where payment for insurance gets taken out of farmers' earnings post-harvest - Agri-input supplier bundles inputs with insurance for a discounted/subsidized price

  • Will there be subsidies for the insurance product? If yes, what percentage of the premium will be covered? Who will provide the subsidy (government, donors, agribusinesses, financial institutions)?

  • Who are the intended beneficiaries of the insurance? Potential answers: smallholder farmers, farmer cooperatives, individual commercial farmers

  • Which regions and crops will the insurance program cover?

  • What is the proposed index-insurance type? Is it weather-based, area-yield, or a hybrid?

docs.title: b. Providers background
docs.text:
These questions will give an overall introduction to the background and structure of the bidding insurance companies.

  • Who is doing the evaluation? e.g., government, agribusiness, agri-input suppliers, broker, etc.

  • What is the company’s core mission and experience in agricultural insurance?

  • What is the company's ownership structure/type? Potential answers: Private, Non-profit, Donor-backed, Government-supported

  • What regions or countries does the company operate in?

  • Who are its primary customers?

  • What is the proposed index-insurance type? Is it weather-based, area-yield, or a hybrid?

docs.title: 2. Payout Value, Size and Frequency
docs.text: This section will look at how much farmers are getting for what they pay and whether insurance companies are getting enough payments to finance payouts using a simple calculator. It will also initiate discussions on the appropriate size and frequency of insurance to set farmer expectations on payouts.

docs.title: a. How much of the money farmers pay is expected to be paid out?
docs.text: Verification through a calculator accessible here

docs.title: b. What is the expected size and frequency of payouts?
docs.text: Visualization of the different scenarios can be done here

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
• How much payout will be based on premium?
  • On average, how big is the gap when payout is lower than what farmers expect?
  • What share of the price would the top up be if all losses could be covered, even the ones the index misses?
  • How good is the quality of the communication with the farmers?
